title: Bonsai Automata
game_overview: An idle zen simulation featuring automated power and irrigation grids to grow bonsais to level 100, combined with reaction-based wilderness excursions.
winning_condition: Successfully discover and cultivate the rarest botanical specimen in the wilderness—the Mythic Golden Ginkgo Bonsai—to Level 100 Mastery in your automated sanctuary.
losing_condition: None. The game is a relaxing zen experience with no fail state or game over. When the expedition backpack reaches maximum capacity, the player simply cannot carry additional items and returns to the starting campsite portal to transport all gathered resources back to the sanctuary.

controls.action: Dig action in the radial shovel minigame during excursions.

controls.input: W/A/S/D or Arrow Keys / Virtual Joystick
controls.action: Move the botanist explorer across the excursion overworld.
Select bonsais to prune, purchase machinery upgrades, and manage inventory slots.
Open inventory and equipment backpack screen.
Switch between Greenhouse Sanctuary and Wilderness Excursion view.

sections.title: Core Mechanics
sections.content: 1. Additive Disrupted Zen Environmental Penalty: Soil degradation compounds additively onto botanical specimens: a tree planted on degraded soil incurs a baseline -10% Growth Speed penalty, with an additional -10% Growth Speed accumulated for each degraded soil tile within its 3x3 halo that is not physically sealed off by a Bamboo Fence (e.g. planted on degraded soil with 2 degraded halo neighbors yields a cumulative -30% Growth Speed penalty). Telemetry consolidates into a single status badge: '⚠️ Disrupted Zen (-X% Growth Speed)'. 2. Calibrated Fabrication Matrix: Standardized recipe durations, energy consumption metrics, and resource costs across all 30 electrical and industrial workbench recipes, aligning fabrication timelines and power draw with engineering tiers.
sections.summary: Additive Disrupted Zen Degradation Dynamics and Calibrated Electrical Crafting.

sections.title: Economy and Progression
sections.content: 1. Industrial Engineering Licenses: Introduced three state-certified fabrication licenses available under the Botanical Market Equipment catalog: T1 License (25 Verdure), T2 License (75 Verdure), and T3 License (200 Verdure). These licenses serve as essential consumable certification components required alongside raw mechanical resources to fabricate advanced automated machinery, sprinkler systems, workbench modules, and rover expedition modules. 2. Standardized Tier Nomenclature: All chassis modifications, workbench overhauls, and rover attachments follow unified T1/T2/T3 nomenclature (T2 Precision Workbench Upgrade, T3 Master Foundry Upgrade, T2 Surveyor Chassis Upgrade, T3 Vanguard Heavy Chassis Upgrade, T1-T3 Storage, Battery, and Radar Modules).
sections.summary: Engineering License Authorization Economy and Standardized Module Nomenclature.
